name: Ascension Cathedral
fact: Built of wood between 1904 and 1907, the cathedral survived the 1911 earthquake that devastated much of the city.

name: Bayterek Monument
fact: The tower’s golden sphere represents the egg of Samruk, a mythical bird that nests in the Tree of Life.

name: Shymqala Citadel
fact: The open-air museum brings Shymkent’s fortified past to life. Excavations at the old town uncovered an eighth-century coin and early medieval pottery.

name: Nur Gasyr Mosque
fact: Four 63-metre minarets frame the central dome of the mosque, which opened in 2008.

name: Miners’ Glory Monument
fact: Two bronze miners lift a piece of coal above their heads in tribute to the workers of the Karaganda coal basin.

name: Karakhan Mausoleum
fact: Local legend links Karakhan’s tomb to nearby Aisha Bibi, whom he is said to have loved.

name: Left Bank Ethnic Village
fact: Kazakh yurts stand alongside recreated homes of communities who lived in eastern Kazakhstan, furnished with objects from the ethnographic museum.

name: Mashkhur Zhusup Mosque
fact: The mosque’s turquoise dome recalls the shanyrak, the circular crown of a traditional Kazakh yurt.

name: Isatay–Makhambet Memorial
fact: The two bronze riders are Isatay Taimanov and the poet Makhambet Utemisuly, leaders of the 1836–1838 uprising.

name: Semey Suspension Bridge
fact: The bridge’s main span stretches 750 metres across the Irtysh between its two towers.

name: Melovoy Lighthouse
fact: Aktau put this octagonal Caspian lighthouse on the roof of an apartment block in 1974.

name: Aitbay Mosque
fact: Built in 1878, the mosque served as a cinema in the 1950s and later reopened as a place of worship.

name: Akhmet Baitursynuly Monument
fact: The seated figure holds a pen, a tribute to the linguist who reformed the Kazakh writing system and wrote early Kazakh-language textbooks.

name: Cathedral of the Archangel Michael
fact: Alexander Pushkin visited the 18th-century cathedral in 1833 while gathering accounts of the Pugachev uprising.

name: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
fact: Timur commissioned the shrine for the Sufi teacher Khoja Ahmed Yasawi. Construction stopped when Timur died in 1405.

name: Abylai Khan Residence
fact: The museum interprets the life of Abylai Khan, whose residence was a meeting place for political negotiations in the 18th century.

name: Kokshetau City History Museum
fact: The museum occupies a turn-of-the-century wooden estate near Lake Kopa. In the courtyard, horse-drawn winter sleds sit alongside a 1930s Cadillac.

name: Historical and Cultural Centre of the First President
fact: The centre pairs exhibits on Kazakhstan’s independence with photographs and objects from Temirtau’s steelmaking history.

name: Muhamedzhan Tynyshpayev Museum
fact: One gallery tells the story of Muhamedzhan Tynyshpayev, a historian and railway engineer who helped build the Turkestan–Siberian Railway.

name: Ekibastuz Museum of Local History
fact: The museum tells how the discovery of coal shaped Ekibastuz and exhibits finds from Stone Age settlements in the surrounding region.

name: Rudny Museum of Local History
fact: The museum puts Rudny’s mining-town history alongside archaeology from the Alekseyevka cultural complex.

name: Monument to the Conquerors of Space
fact: The monument recalls Zhezkazgan’s connection to spaceflight. A Soyuz capsule carrying a three-person crew home from the International Space Station landed southeast of the city in 2018.

name: Nauryzbay Batyr Monument
fact: At Kaskelen’s entrance, a statue by sculptor Nurlan Dalbay depicts the eighteenth-century commander Nauryzbay Batyr on horseback.

name: Zhanaozen City Museum
fact: The museum pairs a history of the city’s founding and the oil industry with yurt furnishings, jewelry and objects from everyday life in Mangystau.

name: Kentau City Museum
fact: Residents helped build the museum’s collection after it opened in 1977. Its mineral specimens trace the story of mining in the Karatau range.

name: Balkhash City Museum of Local History
fact: The museum displays a copper ingot from 1938 alongside exhibitions on the archaeology and wildlife of Lake Balkhash.

name: Shynbolat Dildebayev Miners’ Palace
fact: The building opened as the Baikonur cinema in 1974. It now houses a museum devoted to its namesake, a miner, poet and dombra player.

name: Talhiz Archaeological Site
fact: Excavations at this Silk Roads town uncovered clay masonry inside its defensive wall, along with fragments of pottery and animal bones.

name: Zashagan Mosque
fact: Local fundraising and donations paid for the mosque, which opened in February 2026.

name: Duyseke Ata Mosque
fact: This historic mosque north of Kulsary has several domes over mudbrick walls. It served as a mosque and a school.

name: Saryagash Mineral-Water Resort
fact: The resort in nearby Kokterek grew around warm mineral springs. A clinic opened here to put their waters to therapeutic use.

name: Kosshy Community Centre
fact: The community centre brings a cinema, library, sports hall and workshops for activities from robotics to traditional crafts into one public building.

name: Old Beyneu Underground Mosque
localName: Көне Бейнеудегі Бекет ата жерасты мешіті
fact: Carved into a rocky headland, Beket Ata’s mosque has a round prayer room and shallow niches for lamps.

name: Konaev Municipal Beach No. 5
fact: The city grew up around the Kapshagay hydroelectric project in 1970. Its public beach faces the reservoir that gave the city its former name, Kapchagay.

name: Arys 1 Railway Station
fact: Arys became a major junction when the Turkestan–Siberia Railway entered service in 1930, linking up with the Orenburg–Tashkent line.

name: Zharkent Mosque
fact: Completed in 1895, the mosque pairs a Chinese pagoda roof with Central Asian ornament. Uyghur and Dungan communities funded its construction.

name: Zhetygen Railway Station
fact: Zhetygen is one end of the railway section to Altynkol, a link in the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route.

name: Aksu Ferroalloys Plant
fact: The plant’s smelting shops make chromium, silicon and manganese alloys used to produce different grades of steel.

name: Stepnogorsk Regional History Museum
fact: Inside the Gornyak Palace of Culture, the museum traces the city’s industrial beginnings and displays finds from burial sites at Shondyngkarasy.

name: Lake Shchuchye
fact: This Burabay resort lake takes its name from the pike that live in its waters. It lies in the Ishim River basin.

name: Railway Water Tower
fact: The heritage-listed water tower stands beside Aiteke Bi’s railway station, a reminder of the town’s railway origins.

name: Shu Railway Station
fact: The five-storey passenger station was built in 1989. Its routes connect Shu to cities around Kazakhstan and in Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Russia.

name: Altai Botanical Garden
fact: Set on Sokoliny Hill and the Bystrukha River floodplain, the garden studies native Altai plants and introduces them into cultivation.

name: Zhandarbekov Drama Theatre
localName: Қ. Жандарбеков атындағы Жетісай драма театры
fact: The theatre opened in 1969 with Beimbet Mailin’s musical drama Jalbyr. It was later named for the actor and director Kurmanbek Zhandarbekov.

name: Ayagoz Railway Station
fact: Work began on the station in 1930 as the Turkestan–Siberia Railway reached present-day Ayagoz. A steam-locomotive depot followed.

name: Issyk Museum-Reserve
fact: The reserve protects the Saka burial grounds where archaeologists uncovered the gold-clad figure known as the Golden Man, now a national symbol.

name: Korday Batyr Monument
fact: The village honors Korday Batyr with this statue. A mausoleum dedicated to him stands on Korday Pass.

name: Karlag Memorial Museum
fact: In nearby Dolinka, a museum in the former headquarters of the Karlag forced-labor camp preserves the stories and belongings of prisoners.

name: Fishermen’s Museum
fact: Fishing gear and ship equipment tell the story of the years when Aral was a working fishing port.

name: Okshy Ata Mausoleum
fact: This domed tomb northwest of Shieli is one of seven mausoleums in the Seven Saints memorial complex.

name: Mangistau Railway Station
fact: The first freight train arrived in December 1966, marking the opening of permanent service on the line from Makat to what was then Mangyshlak station.

name: Burlin District History Museum
fact: The museum displays jewelry found in local nomad burials and traces Aksay’s industrial growth around the Karachaganak field.

name: Kandyagash Railway Station
fact: The station building dates to 1984 and serves domestic and international passenger trains.

name: Builders and Miners Monument
localName: Алғашқы құрылысшылар мен кеншілерге арналған ескерткіш
fact: Erected in 1969, this monument honors the first Komsomol builders and miners who worked in Zhitikara.

name: Tole Bi Monument
fact: A statue of the Kazakh judge and statesman Tole Bi stands in Lenger’s landscaped ravine, where a cultural park also displays yurts and traditional swings.

name: Lake Teresken
fact: The sanatorium on the shores of Lake Teresken uses the lake’s silt and mineral-rich brine in its baths and treatments.

name: Igilik Bi Mausoleum
fact: This octagonal adobe mausoleum was built around 1875–1880. It honors Igilik Bi, a local figure who helped develop education and coal mining in the nineteenth century.

name: Ardaqti Ana Museum
fact: This museum opened in 2021 to honor mothers of the Turkistan region. Its designers built the exhibition around women whose work shaped local life.

name: Baizak Batyr Mausoleum
fact: Baizak Batyr’s domed mausoleum overlooks the Talas River. Its tomb incorporates adobe bricks from the earlier burial monument.

name: Almaty Combined Heat and Power Plant No. 3
fact: Construction of the heating and power plant began in 1958. The settlement that grew around it was originally called Energetichesky, a name that reflected its ties to the plant.

name: Soyuz Rocket Monument
fact: The Soyuz launcher on a plinth recalls Baikonur’s role in human spaceflight.

name: Shardara Hydroelectric Station
fact: Commissioned in 1967, Shardara is the last hydroelectric station in the Naryn–Syr Darya cascade.

name: Upper Tobol History and Culture Museum
localName: Лисаков Жоғарғы Тобыл тарихы мен мәдениеті мұражайы
fact: The museum displays Bronze Age objects excavated from the settlement and burial grounds at Lisakovsk, including material from the Andronovo cultures.

name: Sarsenuly Temirbolat Ata Mosque
fact: The mosque opened in June 2024 in Derkul, a settlement administered by Oral. Four carpets are a feature of its prayer hall.

name: Metallurgists’ Monument
fact: This obelisk honors the workers of Khromtau’s metallurgical industry. It is listed among the heritage landmarks of the Aktobe area.

name: Kyzylorda Hydraulic Works
fact: Tasbuget grew around the construction of this dam on the Syr Darya, which helped expand agriculture in the surrounding region.

name: Ilyas Yesenberlin Literary Museum
fact: In the writer’s hometown, the museum preserves Yesenberlin’s manuscripts and a recording of his voice alongside a reconstruction of his study.

name: Talas District Museum
fact: The Talas district museum moved from Akkol to Karatau after Karatau became the district center in 1997.

name: Abay Qunanbaiuly Literary and Memorial Museum
fact: The museum displays a 1933 collection of Abay’s works published in Kyzylorda in Arabic script, along with translations of his Book of Words.

name: Regional Museum of Steppe History
fact: Arkalyk’s steppe history museum welcomed its first visitors in 1973, marking the centenary of the birth of Amangeldi Imanov.

name: Zhanatas Wind Farm
fact: Forty turbines make up the 100-megawatt wind farm south of Zhanatas, near the boundary of the Zhambyl and Turkistan regions.

name: Mukhamedzhan Tynyshpaev Monument
fact: In 2007, Sarkan dedicated this monument to Mukhamedzhan Tynyshpaev, a railway engineer who helped build the Turkestan–Siberian Railway.
